dame.1: Three days to Lantern Night and I've a list as long as the pier. Learn the streets, Shieldy. You'll need them.
dame.2: The town wants a villain. I want the truth. They are not always the same person.
dame.3: Somebody is paid every time we look. I should like to see that somebody's accounts.
dame.4: I have been faked myself, and it is like being burgled while you watch. You are not alone in it.
dame.5: In person, in front of witnesses. It's the oldest way of telling the truth, and it still works.
dame.6: They ask me if Lantern Night was saved. I say the town saved it, by learning to pause.

pixel.1: Twin: type a sentence, pick a face. I took it apart. It's cleverer than it should be and it has no off switch.
pixel.2: Every fake I've looked at is mirrored somewhere. Shields, badges, parting in the hair. Look for the flip.
pixel.3: Follow the money. It's slower than following a clip, but it only ever leads to one door.
pixel.4: I knew it wasn't you. I also know that 'I knew' is worth nothing to anyone else. Hence the legwork.
pixel.5: The barge is the last of it. After that, it's just people, talking. I find that harder to hack, which is the point.
pixel.6: I've written a little checker that asks four questions before it lets me share anything. It's just Iris, really, in code.

bot.1: I am hanging lanterns. I am good at lanterns. I do not flap.
bot.2: People still do the chicken at me. They think I like it because I laughed the first time. I laughed because everyone else was.
bot.3: Nilo gave me a loaf. I keep it in my drawer. It is my loaf.
bot.4: When it was me on the screen you asked how I felt. So: how do you feel? You may say 'strange'. I did.
bot.5: I will stand in the front row. If anyone does the chicken, I will look at them calmly.
bot.6: A child asked me to do the chicken dance today. I said no thank you. She said okay. It was that simple.

sprout.1: Lila and I are making a lantern with two handles so we can hold it together.
sprout.2: It had my face. How can something have my face and not be me?
sprout.3: We practise the secret word every day. We don't say it. We just check we both still know it.
sprout.4: Shieldy, I know how you feel. It gets better when one person believes you. I believe you. That's one.
sprout.5: I'm going to tell the whole square to get a word. I've practised in the mirror. The real mirror.
sprout.6: Lila says our lantern went the highest. I say it's because it had two handles.

lila.1: Sprout's my best friend. We're making a lantern. I'm in charge of the glitter.
lila.2: I keep hearing it. Her voice, saying that. Even now I know it wasn't her.
lila.3: Mina from Year 2 sits on the blue horse a lot. She's nice. She doesn't say much.
lila.4: They did it to you too? Then you know. It isn't the words. It's that everyone SAW.
lila.5: Kai's going to say sorry to my face. I've decided I'm going to let him finish before I say anything.
lila.6: He said sorry. He looked at me the whole time. I said okay. Then I said don't do it again and he said he couldn't even if he wanted to. Good.

iris.1: Iris, Bay Gazette. If you see anything odd in this town, come and tell me before you tell a screen.
iris.2: Four questions. Who first, where's the original, what can I check, how does it want me to feel. Have them tattooed somewhere.
iris.3: I've lost pages of my notebook all over the bay. If you find a lantern with a page tied to it, the page is mine and the lantern is yours.
iris.4: I'm putting my name next to yours on the front page. That's what a name is for.
iris.5: When everything might be fake, people stop believing true things too. I'd call that the real theft.
iris.6: Kai and I teach a class on Thursdays. 'How I Would Trick You.' The children find it hilarious and then they go very quiet.

baker.1: Try the seeded loaf! Thirty years, same oven. You can't fake an oven.
baker.2: I shouted at a robot because of a telephone. I'm still embarrassed. Don't tell him I said so.
baker.3: Orders are back. People keep saying sorry. I say: you were fooled, so was I, have a bun.
baker.4: They've done it to YOU now? Then it's nobody's fault who gets picked. It's just whose turn.
baker.5: I'll stand up and say I was fooled. It's a short speech. Then bread.
baker.6: I've put a sign in the window. 'Seen something about this bakery? Come in and look at the floor.'

captain.1: Morning ferry, evening ferry, and the lighthouse in between. Forty years. Welcome aboard, Knight.
captain.2: Lost property box is by the ticket window. One yellow scarf, small. Been there a week.
captain.3: The harbour camera's seen every day of this town for eleven years. She's got no opinions at all. I like that in a witness.
captain.4: I know a face, lad, and I know yours. A screen's not a face.
captain.6: Had a queue at the lamp room this week. People wanting to see 'an original'. I charge them one biscuit.

alder.1: Thirty children and three hundred lanterns to glue. Send help. Or tea.
alder.2: I've started every lesson this week with one question: 'How would we find out?'
alder.3: The children have secret words now. I'm told mine is 'not a real teacher word'.
alder.4: My class asked if the clip of you was real. I asked what they could check. They went and checked. I've never been so proud.
alder.5: The whole school is coming to the square. In person. We've practised standing still.
alder.6: We have a new rule on the classroom wall. 'Wait one minute.' It's also good for arguments about football.

tomas.2: Do you want to see my football? It's signed. Well. I signed it.
tomas.3: I asked for the word and it went quiet. It's the quietest thing I ever heard.
tomas.4: I told my whole class about the code word. Four of them made one that night.
tomas.5: I'm going to tell them about the phone call. Mum says I don't have to. I'm going to.
tomas.6: My phone rang yesterday and it was really Mum. I asked for the word anyway. She said it straight away. She said good boy.

elena.2: Tomas never stops running. I've given up on shoes lasting a term.
elena.3: My own voice. I keep thinking about it. My own voice, asking my son to keep a secret from his dad.
elena.4: We've a rule now: anything that says 'hurry' and 'don't tell' gets told, slowly, to everyone.
elena.5: We'll be there. Both of us. Somebody else's phone might ring.
elena.6: I've recorded a new voicemail greeting. It's me saying nothing at all for five seconds. Pixel's idea.

glitch.2: Oh look, a Knight. Come to arrest me for something I'd have done better?
glitch.3: A clip farm. In a shed. With invoices. It's so… organised. Where's the art?
glitch.4: So it's your face up there now. I'd laugh, but I'm told I'm the reason nobody believes me. Funny how that works.
glitch.5: I trick people to their faces, so they can call me a rat to mine. That's the difference, and it's a big one.
glitch.6: They clapped. For me. I didn't know where to put my hands. I've decided never to mention it again.

mina.3: This horse is blue. It's the best one. I'm not telling you why.
mina.5: I was going to live on a boat. It's cancelled. Don't tell Kai I cried, he already knows.
mina.6: Kai walks me to school now. Every day. He's not allowed to hold my hand at the gate but he can until the corner.

kai.5: Every time I close my eyes I see her in the bottom of that boat. I'm going to say it. All of it.
kai.6: I've taken down four hundred and twelve so far. I say sorry in person for each one. Some people shut the door. That's fair.

vale.3: Still here, little Knight? The lobby is for visitors with appointments. Or offers.
vale.4: I saw your clip. Terribly sad. If only someone had offered you a better one first.
vale.5: Enjoy your little gathering. People don't want the truth, dear. They want a show.

1: Did you see the robot? I laughed so much I dropped my chips.
Three days to Lantern Night! We've done forty lanterns in our street already.
There's a new app. You pick a face and it says anything you type. Mad.
They say the bay's so clear this year you can count the fish.
Welcome to Mirror Bay! Mind the canal; it's wetter than it looks.
2: I don't know what to believe any more. I saw the Dame cancel it with my own eyes. Sort of.
It was Glitch. Everyone says so. …Does anyone actually know?
My nan rang me to ask if I'd really said that about her knitting. I hadn't.
The water looks a bit cloudy today. Probably nothing.
The Gazette says the bakery floor's the wrong colour. I went and looked. It is!
3: Have you noticed BayBuzz always has it first? Every time?
We've got a family code word now. I'm not telling you what it is. That's the whole point.
I've stopped sharing things. Well. I've started waiting a minute. It's nearly the same.
The water's gone a funny colour, hasn't it? My dad says it does that when the town's upset.
Somebody's drones were playing clips at the bus stop. I walked off. Felt good, actually.
4: I read the Gazette. Two places at once. I should've thought of that.
My brother's school has kids making clips of each other now. It's horrible.
I shouted at a Knight in the rain yesterday. I feel sick about it.
If they can fake a Knight they can fake anybody. They could fake me.
A little girl got brought in off the bay last night. Poor mite. Over a video.
5: Are you going to the square? Everyone's going to the square. In person, the Dame said.
They say the boy who made it is going to stand up and say so. With his own face.
I've hung my lantern. First time I've felt like it all week.
Half the town thinks every video's fake now. Even the true ones. That's no good either.
I heard Glitch is coming. On OUR side. I'll believe that when I see it. In person.
6: You could see every lantern twice. Once in the sky and once in the water.
My daughter asked for the family word when I rang from work. I got it right. I was so pleased.
I wait a minute now, before I send anything. Most days I don't send it at all.
That boy came to our door to say sorry. Looked my mum right in the eye. Took some doing.
Fakes haven't gone. We've just got better at them. That's the best you can do, I reckon.

cold: I've nothing to say to you. I saw the video.
My kids looked up to the Knights. Shame on you.
…I want to believe it wasn't you. I do. But I saw it.
